riskAudit.title: Abuse audit
riskAudit.description: Review request patterns and supporting evidence. Configured rules can automatically ban matching personal and charity model calls.
riskAudit.caveat: Client names and headers are self-reported and may be changed or relayed. A rule match is a lead, not proof of identity or misuse.
riskAudit.comparisonHelp: Compare samples from the same time range and model. A cluster near 125 seconds may reflect a CDN timeout. Generic SDK names, shared limits, mixed clients, and a 200 SPA response do not establish misuse.
riskAudit.noMatch: No sustained match in the observed complete minutes
riskAudit.ipHelp: Only authenticated logical calls with direct or trusted forwarded IPs are associated. Proxy fallback IPs and anonymous scans are excluded; shared networks may contain unrelated people.
riskAudit.matchLimit: Evidence details are limited on this page. Review the paged rule list for further rule definitions.
riskAudit.name: Rule name
riskAudit.ipValuesHelp: Separate IPv4 or IPv6 addresses with newlines, commas or spaces. Up to 64 addresses; duplicates are merged when saved.
riskAudit.ruleHelp: All conditions in a rule must match. Rules are alternatives. Missing or truncated values cannot match. Up to 8 conditions per rule and 1,000 rules.
riskAudit.autoBan: Automatic ban for new model calls
riskAudit.autoBanInvalid: Enter a whole duration from 1 second to 3,650 days.
riskAudit.autoBanHelp: New matching personal and charity model calls are refused before dispatch. Historical scans and discovery do not trigger bans.
riskAudit.configHelp: Risk uses total user occupancy and the limit at the time. Restarts, missing records, unsettled requests, or changed or unknown limits restart the consecutive exceedance count.
riskAudit.distribution: Client distribution on this source page
riskAudit.scanHelp: Each step scans up to 100 logical requests. An empty match page does not mean the entire selected period has no matches.
riskAudit.accessHelp: Anonymous events are site totals and never attributed to an account. A zero generation denominator gives an unknown ratio. Access events do not count toward generation RPM or shared-IP risk.
riskAudit.partialAssociations: Only the first 24 user/type associations are shown.
riskAudit.rangeHelp: Quick ranges use server time. The default is 24 hours, or the configured shared-IP window.
riskAudit.invalidRange: Choose a valid past range of up to 30 days. Quick ranges avoid differences between your clock and the server.
riskAudit.observations: Recorded minutes only; missing time is not treated as zero usage
riskAudit.latestObservations: Latest 100 minute records; the summary uses all available records in this range
riskAudit.ruleSteps: Create and enable a rule, then open Client matches to review matching requests. Saved rules are evaluated automatically when you view the selected period.
riskAudit.templateHelp: Client presets fill observed self-reported markers; review and save to enable them. New API and One API titles do not require a fixed website. These markers occur only on some relay paths; derivatives can match if they retain them. Hidden or changed markers need another observed rule. The custom website-and-title pattern requires both fields.

gatewayCapabilities.title: Gateway model capabilities
gatewayCapabilities.description: Declare verified capabilities for an exact Gateway URL and upstream model. Changes apply to new requests immediately, including normal and flattened calls.
gatewayCapabilities.emptyBody: Add a verified target when it needs reasoning, output, storage or cache controls.
gatewayCapabilities.targetHint: Copy the URL and complete model name from the binding. Both must match; trailing URL slashes are removed when saved.
gatewayCapabilities.adapterHint: Choose the adapter used by this upstream model. Saving a declaration does not test the provider or prove that it honored a request.
gatewayCapabilities.effortsHint: Select only verified levels. No selection rejects explicit reasoning-effort controls.
gatewayCapabilities.outputHint: Tokens. 0 means no declared ceiling. A positive ceiling keeps the requested output budget and rejects larger requests; it does not replace the caller's budget.
gatewayCapabilities.outputAnthropicHint: Tokens. Anthropic requires a positive ceiling. It keeps the requested output budget and rejects larger requests; it does not replace the caller's budget.
gatewayCapabilities.storageHint: The default rejects an explicit store control. OpenAI mapping forwards it to the verified OpenAI adapter.
gatewayCapabilities.omitWarning: Omitting store:false sends no storage instruction upstream. It does not guarantee that the provider will avoid retention.
gatewayCapabilities.cacheHint: Anthropic preserves explicit cache points and TTLs. The final cache point option places automatic caching on the last eligible content block. Cache hits depend on the upstream.
gatewayCapabilities.absent: No capabilities declared for this target; explicit capability controls may be rejected.
gatewayCapabilities.deleteDescription: Remove the declaration for {{model}} at {{baseUrl}}. New requests lose these declared capabilities; requests already running keep their settings.

cache.label: Automatic cache default
cache.help: For Gateway only. Caller cache marks on the request, text or tools take priority. The provider decides cache hits. Saved defaults stay hidden; keep them or choose again.
cache.inherited: The cache default inherits with the body defaults. Choosing “Set here” replaces the entire defaults section.

editor.title: Request headers and body
editor.description: Configure only fields supported by the selected connector. Saved values are hidden after saving.
editor.openaiSupport: OpenAI-compatible endpoints use native Chat Completions and Responses requests. Exclude an unsupported client field explicitly, then set any replacement field here.
editor.convertedSupport: Anthropic and Gateway convert supported OpenAI fields. Extra client fields reach the native request only when their paths are declared below.
editor.allSupport: These settings apply to each eligible connection. OpenAI-compatible requests preserve bounded extensions; Anthropic and Gateway require native extension paths to be declared.
editor.listHelp: One name or JSON Pointer per line. Duplicate or unsafe entries are rejected.
editor.bodyHelp: Path: /temperature; value: 0.7. Text requires JSON quotes, for example /reasoning_effort with "low". Nested paths use /thinking/budget_tokens with 4096. Defaults fill missing fields; forced values overwrite them.
editor.fixedHelp: Enter a header name such as User-Agent, with no leading slash or colon. Its value is plain text, for example MyClient/1.0. This overrides the forwarded value after abuse checks. Saved values are hidden.
editor.name: Header or path
editor.stale: The displayed settings could not be refreshed and may be stale. Refresh successfully before saving.
editor.saveError: Could not save request adaptation. Check the fields and retry after refreshing.
editor.unknown: The save outcome is uncertain. Refresh before trying again.
editor.conflict: The configuration changed. Refresh before editing again.
editor.invalidJSON: Enter a valid JSON value for each changed body field.
editor.duplicate: Names and paths must be unique within each section.
editor.readOnly: This setting is read-only for your role.
editor.protectedPathsHelp: One relative JSON Pointer per line, such as /token or /credentials/0/key. Select strings only.
editor.protectionHelp: Use for secrets, not ordinary options. A matching response is stopped; streaming fragments already sent cannot be recalled.
editor.geminiSupport: Gemini supports Chat. Native settings are limited to thinkingConfig and safetySettings; set the output budget with Chat token parameters.
editor.responsesSupport: Responses is native. Chat Completions uses limited conversion; unsupported fields are rejected before calling the upstream.
editor.decisionsSupport: Decisions uses its own JSON endpoint. Streaming and native extensions are unavailable.
editor.chatCompletionsSupport: Chat Completions is native. Responses uses limited conversion; unsupported fields are rejected before calling the upstream.
editor.systemOneSupport: System One uses its own messages and usage format.
editor.rerankSupport: Rerank uses the selected provider's supported request fields. Unsupported fields are rejected before calling the upstream.

service.title: Request rewriting
service.description: Add headers and parameters for this service. Saved values remain hidden.
service.listHelp: One header name or /parameter path per line.
service.bodyHelp: Path: /temperature; value: 0.7. Text requires JSON quotes, for example /reasoning_effort with "low". Nested paths use /thinking/budget_tokens with 4096. Defaults fill missing fields; forced values overwrite them.
service.fixedHelp: Enter a header name such as User-Agent, with no leading slash or colon. Its value is plain text, for example MyClient/1.0. This overrides the forwarded value after abuse checks. Saved values are hidden.

personal.personalDescription: These rules apply only to this model. Each section inherits the selected service by default. “Set here” replaces that entire section; an empty section turns it off for this model.
personal.inheritedEndpoint: Uses the service selected for each request.
personal.excludedHelp: One top-level parameter name per line, such as temperature or max_tokens, without a slash. These fields are removed before optional parameter validation. Do not also set them in defaults, forced values or native extensions (including inherited service settings). Routing, input and response protocol fields cannot be excluded.
personal.headerListHelp: One header name per line, for example X-Client-Version. No slash, colon or value. Only listed client headers are forwarded.
personal.nativeListHelp: One parameter path per line, for example /thinking. For Anthropic or Gateway this permits that extra JSON field to enter the native upstream request. The field and value must be supported by that upstream.

model.title: Request adaptation
model.saveHelp: Save these changes separately from model settings.

mfa.accountDescription: Add an authenticator to protect browser access to your account. API calls using your CallerKey keep working as usual.
mfa.requiredPolicy: Your current account level requires an authenticator. You cannot turn it off.
mfa.setupDescription: Scan the QR code with Microsoft Authenticator, Okta Verify, or another TOTP authenticator.
mfa.verifyDescription: Enter your authenticator code to continue. Verification lasts 7 days in this login session.
mfa.qrUnavailable: The QR code could not be displayed. Use the manual setup key below.
mfa.manualHelp: Choose a time-based code. Keep this key private.
mfa.codeHelp: Enter the six-digit code shown in your authenticator.
mfa.freshCodeHelp: Wait for a new code if you just used the current one.
mfa.lostAuthenticator: Lost your authenticator? Contact an administrator to reset it.
mfa.invalidCode: That code is incorrect or has already been used. Try the next code.
mfa.setupExpired: This setup has expired. Start again to get a new QR code and key.
mfa.rateLimited: Too many incorrect codes. Wait 15 minutes before trying again.
mfa.conflict: The authenticator settings changed. Check the current status and try again.
mfa.disableDescription: Your account will no longer ask for an authenticator code. Enter a fresh code to confirm.
mfa.disableRequired: Your current account level requires an authenticator. You cannot turn it off.
mfa.verifiedUntil: Verified in this login session until {{time}}.
mfa.requiredError: Verify your authenticator to continue. Your input has been kept.
mfa.recoveryDescription: Authenticator verification is needed to continue. Your input has been kept.
mfa.recovered: Verification complete. Review your input and submit the action again.
mfa.adminDescription: Reset a lost authenticator so the user can set it up again.
mfa.resetDescription: Reset the authenticator for {{user}} and sign out all of their browser sessions. They must sign in again. Their CallerKey stays unchanged.
mfa.resetDone: Authenticator reset. All browser sessions were signed out. The user must sign in again.
